correctness.rationale: The claim is finite and reconstructed from the definition. The standalone verifier exhaustively enumerates all unordered seven-column families over the 63 nonzero six-bit columns using only collision-equivalent pruning, finds exactly 30, and exhaustively finds no eight-column family. It then directly recomputes all singleton/pair Boolean ORs for every maximum, establishes one S6 orbit and stabilizer 24, and verifies the matching/parity structure and the seven-point Steiner triple system extension. Because every subfamily of a separable family is separable, the absence of size 8 proves the maximum is 7. No timeout, sampling, or floating-point inference is used.

originality.rationale: The closest exact-parameter primary source proves a Fano-derived optimum but not equality-case rigidity. Exact-claim and alias searches found no statement implying that every six-test seven-item at-most-two separable design is Fano-derived, nor the counts 30 and 151,200 or the single-orbit conclusion. The nearest database records concern different properties (rank-three fooling-set matrices, a general separable-to-disjunct conversion frontier, and constant-weight cover-free families) and do not imply this classification.
residual_risks: An obscure or unindexed historical source could contain the same equality classification; no implication-equivalent statement was found in the inspected exact-parameter source or the recorded searches.

value.rationale: This is the complete equality classification at the historically singled-out first seven-item optimum: the exact source is explicitly about obtaining the best tests for seven items and at most two defectives. The new result identifies all optima, gives exact labeled counts and symmetry, and explains the Fano construction as forced rather than merely available. That is a natural structural endpoint for the known sharp parameter, not an arbitrary slice or a routine recomputation of the optimum.
